Kept under Law 5 — the array was a second copy of the journal, but these words were not: measured 2026-09-10, 66 of 79 stored notes appeared nowhere else in either root, and they carry Akien's verbatim approvals, back-edge reasons and ruling citations. Verbatim: THE BOAT CROSSED ITSELF, and that is the claim. No hand fired a crossing: `cairn test --seal` sealed the proof green, the tester announced the seal, codemother heard it, resolved the four coordinates, and asked the harbor — which cleared it. The journal reads actor codemother, cleared_by codemother, at 2026-09-09T21:46:05, and the whole exchange is on the bus record: tester --sealed--> codemother (accepted true), codemother --clear--> harbor_master, harbor_master --clear reply--> codemother (accepted true). THE FIRST LIVE FIRE FOUND THE SEAM COULD NOT WORK AT ALL, which no green proof had said: `_announce_seals` reached only codemother, and because `reach` wires a synchronous delivery hook, codemother handled the seal inside the TESTER's process, where harbor_master was not wired — every boat refused, and the command still printed a clean SEALED. Coupled to it, the in-memory ring was never flushed, so an envelope the hook did not handle was in no channel afterwards at all: neither acted on nor recoverable. Both fixed, and the reason no tooth caught them is the finding worth keeping — the harness stubbed `reach` with `lambda *_devices: bus`, swallowing the one thing the call says. The instrument could not fail on the defect it guards; the underscore was the whole of it (Law 8). THE SECOND FIRE WAS REFUSED FOR A HONEST REASON and that is the design working: the harbor red the build_inspector on codemother (1 finding of 34 checks) because the previous commit's own pre-commit reseal had left four validation files uncommitted. Nothing was journaled, the refusal named the finding, the finding named the file.
